core_obligations: Attach a class xi_F in H^1(C, H) to an H-torsor F: form the free abelian sheaf Z[F] on F, its augmentation sigma to the constant sheaf Z, the canonical map a from Ker(sigma) to H sending [s] - [s'] to the unique local section h with h.s' = s, push the displayed short exact sequence out along a, and take the boundary of the global section 1 of Z in the long exact cohomology sequence of the lower row (proof lines 299-333).

Recover a torsor from an arbitrary class: choose an embedding of H into an injective abelian sheaf I, set Q = I/H, use H^1(C, I) = 0 to lift xi to a global section q of Q, and take the subsheaf of sets F of I of sections mapping to q, which is then an H-torsor (proof lines 336-356).

Establish that the two constructions are mutually inverse, which the author states at proof lines 358-360 and leaves to the reader in the sentence printed verbatim in the delivered item; the card records this as the author's own declared omission rather than supplying a replacement argument.
proof_roadmap: From a torsor to a class: the free abelian sheaf Z[F] and its augmentation sigma have kernel generated by the sections [s] - [s'], and the torsor action defines a canonical map a from that kernel onto H (proof lines 299-313).

Pushout and boundary: pushing the short exact sequence 0 to Ker(sigma) to Z[F] to Z to 0 out along a yields an extension 0 to H to E to Z to 0, and the boundary operator applied to the global section 1 of Z gives the class xi_F in H^1(C, H) (proof lines 313-333).

From a class to a torsor: embed H into an injective I, put Q = I/H, lift xi to q in H^0(C, Q) because H^1(C, I) vanishes, and take the subsheaf of sets of I of sections mapping to q (proof lines 336-356).
The author closes by stating that the verification that these constructions are mutually inverse is omitted (proof lines 358-360).
difficulty_reason: The statement identifies two objects that are built by completely different means: isomorphism classes of H-torsors on a site and the first cohomology group H^1(C, H) of an abelian sheaf (statement lines 292-295). The proof has to construct both directions explicitly. The first construction is a pushout followed by a boundary operator: it forms the free abelian sheaf on the torsor, its augmentation sigma, the map a from Ker(sigma) to H determined by the torsor action through h.s' = s, pushes the sequence defining Z[F] out along a, and takes the image of 1 under the connecting homomorphism (proof lines 299-333). The second is a representability argument that needs an injective embedding, the vanishing of H^1 of an injective sheaf, and the identification of the preimage of a global section of Q = I/H as a torsor (proof lines 336-356). What the author does not do is verify that the two constructions are mutually inverse; that verification is declared omitted at proof lines 358-360 and is retained verbatim in the delivered item, so the bijection itself is asserted by the author and not carried out in the printed argument.
